title: The house beside San Jacinto Hall and his sisters
summary: He grew up next to the building that became San Jacinto Hall, remembering the neighbours' children. He says he has two younger sisters and no brothers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, this particular thing that I'm talking about, it was my aunt that gave the dance herself, you see. That's how I come to, you know, be really interested. I remember, I'll tell you another thing, I remember when a lot of bands they used to be playing, they was going to the, you know the economy hall? The very street hall used to turn, we used to live right next to where the San Jacinto is, that great big brown house.
Well John Slaseby said something you told him that you were there when they built San Jacinto?

Oh yes, I was living right next door. In San Jacinto it was a big, it was a, you could see it had been a fine home, the house, there was some German people, I don't recall their last name, but I know the boy's name, he was around my age, I mean the boy was around my age, his name was Norman. He had an older sister by the name of Yvonne, very very pretty girl and my mama named my sister after her, named my baby sister Yvonne, right after her. And my baby sister was born in 15 and I remember that well.
Oh by the way, I keep changing the subject, do you have any brothers or anything?
No brothers, I have two sisters. Two sisters. I am the oldest. I have a sister, a few years younger than, I think about six or seven years younger. It's just three of us all together, that's all.
Well go ahead about this hall, what year did you build that about?
Oh this, I don't recall, I really don't recall what year it was built.
Let's see, you were born in 1909? I'm born in 1909.

Nine. I don't recall, I know when the San Jose Center they bought the building and they had their… Before 1920 then I guess. I don't really recall, I really don't recall, but I know they bought the building and later years there the building was knocked down and they built their club and everything. I did remember that.
Still they have dances there sometimes. They do huh?
On Sunday nights. Oh yeah, that's September so in 1929, I mean in 1915, that was my birthday, I was six years old that day.

Boy I remember a lot of incidents of when I was riding a bike up and down the house, my grandmother slapped me, you know some old people that took the bike and put it in there, and they were kneeling praying. But you know we didn't have sense enough to know any danger. It was a heck of a stone because I remember the mailman passing the tomate antibody.
